items.title: Sudan: Alleged 'Arrest' of ICC Fugitive Ahmed Haroun in Doubt
items.description: [Dabanga] Amsterdam -- Politicians and activists have questioned widespread reports, covered on Sunday in international media including the Associated Press and Reuters and attributed to unnamed sources, that Ahmed Haroun, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court (ICC), has been arrested. The reports emerged following his appearance in a recorded interview with Sudan Podcast on Friday. items.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopia Committed to Collective Security, Says Major General Adamneh
items.description: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia remains committed to collective security with professionalism, discipline and sacrifice, Defense Peacekeeping Center Head Major General Adamneh Mengiste said.
items.titleIt: Ethiopia: Ethiopia Committed to Collective Security, Says Major General Adamneh

items.title: Ethiopia: Food Shortages Hit 71 Percent of Ethiopian Families Displaced Into Kenya's Moyale
items.description: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Tens of thousands of people who fled escalating conflict in Moyale along Ethiopia's border between Oromia and Somali regional states and crossed into northern Kenya are facing acute food shortages, inadequate shelter and limited access to clean water and healthcare, according to a new assessment by the International Organization for Migration (IOM) and humanitarian partners.
items.titleIt: Ethiopia: Food Shortages Hit 71 Percent of Ethiopian Families Displaced Into Kenya's Moyale

items.title: Up to 50,000 Ethiopians flee to Kenya as clashes escalate
items.description: Ongoing clashes on the Ethiopian side have forced thousands of people to cross into Kenya seeking safety since 22 October. The UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) is closely monitoring the situation on the Kenya–Ethiopia border in Moyale.
items.titleIt: Up to 50,000 Ethiopians flee to Kenya as clashes escalate

items.title: Egypt: Seven dead, 125 injured in collision between two trains
items.description: Rail workers began repairing damaged tracks in Al-Ayyat, Egypt, on Monday 9 November, a day after two passenger trains collided south of Cairo, killing seven people and injuring at least 125 others.
items.titleIt: Egypt: Seven dead, 125 injured in collision between two trains

items.title: From Abu Dhabi to Beledweyne: Sanbaloolshe Names Irro, Deni and Madobe in Opposition Alliance Claims
items.description: On November 6, two prominent political figures arrived in Beledweyne accompanied by armed escorts, intensifying a confrontation over Hirshabelle's leadership. items.title: Somalia's Eritrean-trained naval chief appointment risks further straining ties with Ethiopia
items.description: Mohamed Abdulqadir "Shariif" has been appointed commander of the Somali Navy and Coastal Defence Forces, replacing Brig. Gen. Abdiwahab Omar. His military training in Eritrea comes at a sensitive time for the region, with relations between Ethiopia and Eritrea deteriorating and renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia raising fears of a wider confrontation.  The appointment could cause concern in Addis Ababa, particularly as Somalia has strengthened its engagement with Eritrea and Egypt amid longstanding disputes with Ethiopia over sovereignty, regional security and access to the Red Sea.
